changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6625-retire-fieldmeta-decimals.md`

- names `GridField.tsx` → `packages/fields/src/widgets/GridField.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `buildFieldMeta` computed `decimals: overrides.decimals ?? meta?.decimals ?? meta?.scale` on **every** call and the value **reached nothing**. Re-measured on this branch's base (`efdc6c62`): **zero `.decimals` member reads** across `@object-ui/fields`, `@object-ui/i18n`, `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/core` and `plugin-dashboard` itself — the only non-comment occurrence was the write being removed here. The **positive control in the same query shape** fires: `.scale` member reads hit `NumberField.tsx`, `GridField.tsx` and `fields/src/index.tsx`. So the zero is a finding, not a broken query. The `overrides.decimals ??` head of that chain had already lost its only feeder when objectui#6425's ruling removed the authored read from `ObjectDataTable.enrich()`; `RecordDetailDrawer`, the only other `buildFieldMeta` caller, passes no overrides at all. Both halves retire together, so the key leaves in one move.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `6f864cf62` (merge-base with origin/main): 6 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1822 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2432 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36744953591)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `587c35168e9395ac40fcf6f5840e432b66ed26cc`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card objectui#10783 (body and all four comments: triage `5857095378`, unlock `5904370405`, claim `5913969854`, os-dev-report `5915518804`), PR #11238 (body, 8-file list, the diff against `main` at the head), and the head's check-runs read with `filter=latest`. Source confirmations were reads only: objectui files at the head through the contents API, and objectstack `origin/main` (`1741c5dcb6`) `packages/spec` through `git show`.

**Check-runs on the head:** 43 with `filter=latest`, all completed when judged (ten were still in progress when this review started; waited in the foreground until the last shard finished): 40 `success`, 3 `skipped` (`dependabot`, `Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard ...)` — lanes this PR does not trigger), 0 failed. The gate families this diff derives are green by name: `Lint`, `Type Check`, `Test` (all eight shards and `dist pins`), `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Changeset Declaration` / `Bump Policy` / `Fixed Group Check` / `Overwrite Report` / `Claim Re-read`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Shell Escape Residue Scan`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build & E2E`.

### ① Derived judgments

Binding direction (triage `5857095378`, rulings B on objectstack#19629 and 乙 on objectstack#19910): the currency's ISO 4217 minor unit decides a currency column's width; `currencyWidth` drops `c.scale`; the hydrated case is REPORTED, never silently dropped, default site `objectui validate`.

1. **The re-measure — right.** The PR's 17.5.0 table matches the schema at source: objectstack `origin/main` `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` `InlineGridColumnSchema` carries a `superRefine` that adds an issue at `['scale']` when `column.type === 'currency' && column.scale !== undefined`, with the comment 「Reach, deliberately: only the DECLARED `type` is visible here」. So the typed column is refused, the identity-only column parses, and `number` keeps `scale`. The unlock scan `5904370405` had already probed the published 17.5.0 the same way.
2. **`currencyWidth` no longer reads the column — right.** The diff changes its signature to `currencyWidth(currency)` and both callers follow: `storedFractionScale` (the stored face, reached from the exported `computeRow`) and `currencyText` (the shown face). `storedFractionScale` still returns `c.scale` for every non-currency type, so the `number` control is unchanged. Public surface: `GridColumn.scale` keeps its type (docblock only), `computeRow`'s signature is unchanged, `currencyWidth` was never exported. Accept set of `@object-ui/fields`: unchanged; a currency column's `scale` is still accepted by the type and now decides nothing. Behaviour change, documented: JPY 0 / USD 2 / KWD 3 on both faces, pinned in `GridField.currencyScaleNotRead-10783.test.tsx` with rows where the minor unit and the old `scale`-first read disagree, plus the `number` control. Docblocks at `GridColumn.scale`, `currencyWidth`, `storedFractionScale` and `currencyText` now say the minor unit decides and cite the two rulings — the three docblocks the card named are corrected.
3. **The report site — measurement sound, channel accepted as the named fallback, gap escalated (see ③).** Confirmed at source, reads only: (a) objectstack `origin/main` `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` `FormViewSchema.subforms[]` declares `columns: z.array(z.any()).optional()`; (b) the objectui mirror `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` `object-form` `subforms[]` declares the same `columns: z.array(z.any())`, and `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts` judges the document through `safeValidateSchema` from `@object-ui/types/zod` and nothing else; (c) `packages/app-shell/src/providers/MetadataProvider.tsx` `attachInlineSubforms` relays a relationship field's `inlineColumns` into `subforms[].columns` at runtime; (d) `MasterDetailForm.tsx` resolves the child through `dataSource.getObjectSchema(d.childObject)` and then `deriveDetail(...)`, whose `columns` is `hydrateColumns(override.columns, childSchema)` — the one choke point where the child field's type meets the authored column (`LineItemsPanel` receives already-hydrated columns). The PR body's positive control is the right shape: the same document with `childObject: 5` is refused at `subforms.0.childObject`, so the validator reached `subforms` and the green on `columns` is a reading. I did not re-run it (read-only). Is a `console.warn` a loud channel? It is the repository's own author-diagnostic channel — `sectionFields.ts` carries three module-level-`Set` once-per-site `console.warn` reports of exactly this shape, and `MasterDetailForm` warns the same way when a child schema fails to load — and the report names the column, the child object, the key and the remedy, and its first sentence is the spec's refusal (`INLINE_GRID_CURRENCY_SCALE_REFUSAL`, 「`scale` is not valid on a `currency` inline grid column — delete the key.」). It is not a silent drop: the key is named at the first place it is knowable. It is weaker than the default site, because an author who never opens a browser console sees nothing; the dev says so itself and escalates a static refusal (open question 1). Both arms are covered: the identity-only column (hydrated, the card's case) and a declared currency column reaching hydration unjudged through `subforms[].columns`. Pinned in `deriveMasterDetail.currencyScale-10783.test.ts`: reported once naming column and child object, stored at the minor unit under JPY and KWD, once across two resolves, with a no-`scale` control and a hydrates-to-`number` control that is not reported and still decides. Residual, not blocking: the report is skipped when the child schema carries no `fields` (the function's early return), a degenerate case where nothing hydrates anyway.
4. **The two replaced objectui#10355 pins — right.** Both rows asserted the branch the ruling reversed (`scale` winning on the stored value; `scale` deciding the display). Each is retired with a comment naming what stood there and where the reversal is pinned, following that file's own objectui#10071 retirement comment. The first half of the display row (a stored amount with more places shows at the yen's width) is kept as its own test. **The fixture — right:** `GridField.test.tsx` `computed columns` declared `type: 'currency'` with `scale: 2`, which 17.5.0 refuses; its two assertions (`amount: 40`, a dash for blank inputs) resolve no currency and produce the same values with or without the key. **The dated note on the pending objectui#10355 changeset — allowed and true.** A changeset body publishes verbatim into the CHANGELOG at the next release, and 10355 is pending in this same release; the file already carries the 2026-09-29 note objectui#11073 appended for the same reason, and the two changeset gates that read bodies (`Changeset Claim Re-read`, `Changeset Overwrite Report`) are green on the head. Checked sentence by sentence against the file at the head: list item 1 (「its authored `scale`, when it has one」) and 「Columns with an authored `scale` ... round as before」 are now false for currency columns; the 2026-09-29 note is about that same authored width and no longer holds; 17.5.0 refuses the key on a declared currency column (confirmed at source); `number` is unchanged. Nothing else in the body is contradicted.
5. **Ablation legs — sound.** `currencyWidth` no longer takes the column, so the mutation site moved to its two callers, one per face; that is the only faithful restoration. Stored leg: 4 red (three stored rows plus the plugin-form hydrated-width pin, which goes through `computeRow`) and the `number` controls and every report pin green — consistent, because `storedFractionScale` returns before the mutated line for non-currency columns and the report does not read the width. Shown leg: 3 red (the display rows only). Each leg red only on its own face, as predicted before the run. Restores proven against the HEAD blob `719fc0b8`, which is the blob the diff index line names.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/10783-grid-currency-scale-not-read.md`: `@object-ui/fields` minor, `@object-ui/plugin-form` patch. Against the diff: `fields` changes observable behaviour (an authored key on a currency column stops deciding the width, with a stated before/after `¥1,234.57` → `¥1,235`) and moves no public type or signature; under this repository's version-alignment rule (AGENTS.md: objectui's own breaking changes are marked `minor`, a `major` never enters the fixed group) `minor` with the Behaviour change paragraph is the right level, and `patch` would understate it. `plugin-form` adds a console diagnostic and no API — `patch` is right. Both packages sit in the one `fixed` group, so the group's bump is `minor` either way; the split is documentary and matches the diff. The body's claims match the code: the identity-only column still parses; the declared column is reported because `subforms[].columns` is unjudged; the column still renders at the minor unit. `check-changeset-presence`, `no-major`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy` and `Changeset Fixed Group Check` are green on the head.

`Clause-②:` the PR body says `no`; the claim `5913969854` said `no (narrowing)`. My reading of the built diff: `no`. No objectui accept set moves — `GridColumn` still admits `scale` on any column, `safeValidateSchema` passes exactly what it passed, and the added report is a warning that refuses nothing. The claim's `(narrowing)` rested on `objectui validate` reporting the hydrated case, and that premise fell to the measurement in ①.3. The behaviour change is a semantic change to what an accepted key does, not a narrowing of what is accepted; the changeset carries it. The dev disclosed the divergence in the PR body's second line and in the report. Whether the role file's verbatim-copy rule still binds after a measured premise change is the seat's call (open question 2); on the diff itself `no` is the true line.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **`deriveMasterDetail.ts` in the diff, outside the claim's named files — accepted.** The claim named the report site only as 「where the column is judged」 and asked the dev to 「say where it went」; the dev measured (①.3), took the dispatch-named fallback, said where it went, and touched no `packages/cli` file, so draft PR objectui#11069's hunks (`validate.ts`, `check.ts`, `authoring-face.ts`, `union-arm-diagnostics.ts`) are untouched. The file is `domain:ui`.
2. **Ablation at the callers rather than inside `currencyWidth` — accepted** (①.5): the function no longer takes the column.
3. **Dated note on the objectui#10355 changeset and the spec-illegal fixture key — accepted** (①.4).
4. **No-break-space repair and the three lock queue-timeouts — accepted;** every reading in the report is from a completed run at the head, and the head's `Control Byte Scan` and `Shell Escape Residue Scan` are green.
5. **Open question 1 (a spec-side refinement refusing `inlineColumns[].scale` on a column naming a sibling `currency` field, option B) — escalate as a card for objectstack `domain:spec`, not Acceptance notes.** The fact is statically known in the object document `os validate` judges (`inlineColumns` sits on the child object's own relationship field, and the sibling field it names is in the same document), the spec's own `superRefine` comment records the current reach as a deliberate stop at the declared `type`, and Acceptance notes in an objectui PR reach nobody who can change `packages/spec`. Filing it is the seat's, not this record's; the card should cite objectstack#20045 and PR #20223, the reach comment in `InlineGridColumnSchema`, and the zero-producer measurements (objectstack#20045; this PR). Not blocking: this PR's render-time report stays the backstop for the `subforms[].columns` path, which such a refinement cannot reach.
